title: Unveiling dust, molecular gas, and high star-formation efficiency in extremely UV bright star-forming galaxies at z ∼ 2.1─3.6
question: How much dust, cold molecular gas, obscured star formation, depletion time and star-formation efficiency do 12 extremely UV-bright starburst galaxies at z = 2.08-3.61 have

data.bands: Band 3 (CO line) and Band 6 (1.3 mm / 240 GHz continuum)

what.value: CO excitation corrections r31 = 0.77 +/- 0.14 and r41 = 0.61 +/- 0.13

evidence.loc: From the CO emission line to molecular gas masses
evidence.quote: we applied the CO luminosity correction factors $r_{3,1} = 0.77\pm 0.14$ and $r_{4,1} = 0.61\pm 0.13$, respectively, derived by (cite: Boogaard+20)

what.value: UV, spectroscopic and stellar-population properties of the targets (z_nebular, M_UV, beta_UV, metallicities, ages) from previous work for 7/12 targets

evidence.quote: The rest-frame UV and optical properties of a fraction (7/12) of these targets were analysed in detail in previous works

external_data.citation: (cite: Marques+20b; Marques+21; Marques+22; Marques+24; Alvarez+21; Upadhyaya+24)

what.value: T_dust = 40 K assumed for the starburst dust

evidence.loc: From the FIR dust continuum to IR luminosities and dust masses
evidence.quote: We assumed $T_{\rm dust} = 40~\rm K$ for the dust associated with the starburst regions of our targets

what.value: Dust opacity law beta = 1.4, kappa_0 = 40 cm2/g at lambda_0 = 100 um

evidence.loc: From the FIR dust continuum to IR luminosities and dust masses
evidence.quote: we assumed $\beta = 1.4$, $\kappa_0 = 40~\rm cm^2~g^{-1}$, and $\lambda_0 = 100$ $\mu$m (cite: BianchiSchneider07)

what.value: Seven kappa dust-composition models used to set L_IR and M_dust uncertainties

evidence.loc: From the FIR dust continuum to IR luminosities and dust masses
evidence.quote: seven different $\kappa$ models of dust composition listed in (cite: Ginolfi+19)

what.value: UV SFR conversion kappa_UV = 1.3e-28 Msun/yr per (erg/s/Hz) from BPASS binary models

evidence.quote: derived using the Binary Population and Spectral Synthesis (BPASS) binary models (cite: Eldridge+17; StanwayEldridge18; Byrne+22)

what.value: Dust production model M_dust = (0.004 +/- 0.002) M_stars for SNe (Chabrier IMF)

evidence.quote: derived $\mu_{\rm dust} = 0.004\pm 0.002$ for the (cite: Chabrier03) IMF

recipe.goal: calibrate and image ALMA band 6 continuum and band 3 CO cubes
recipe.method: Standard ALMA pipeline calibration, then CASA tclean imaging (MFS continuum over four spws; CO cubes of all channels), cleaned to 4x dirty-image RMS, then primary beam correction
key_parameters: Pixel size 0.1'' / 0.15'' (continuum) and 0.1'' / 0.05'' (CO); natural weighting for continuum; Briggs robust 1.0 or natural for CO; threshold 4x RMS

recipe.goal: build CO moment-0 maps and spectra and measure I_CO, z_CO, FWHM
recipe.method: immoments over the optimum channel range (maximising S/N of the 1D spectrum extracted in a custom polygonal aperture), multi-component Gaussian fits to the spectra; upper limits from 4 sigma RMS over ~350 km/s for non-detections
key_parameters: Custom (polygonal) aperture including all flux above the RMS and typically bigger than the beam; no aperture correction

recipe.goal: convert CO flux to L'_CO and molecular gas mass
recipe.method: L'_CO from Solomon+97 Eq. 3; M_molgas = alpha_CO * L'_CO / r_J1
assumptions: alpha_CO = 1 Msun/(K km/s pc2) (nearby starburst value); MW value 4.36 discussed as alternative

recipe.goal: measure 1.3 mm continuum fluxes and FIR sizes
recipe.method: Aperture photometry on the primary-beam-corrected maps; elliptical 2D Gaussian fits in the uv plane with GILDAS UV_FIT; Reff,FIR from deconvolved FWHMs; 4 sigma upper limits from dirty-image RMS for non-detections
key_parameters: Free parameters: centre, flux, FWHM major, FWHM minor, position angle; Reff,FIR = half-emission radius from the circularised FWHM

recipe.goal: derive L_IR and dust masses from the single 1.3 mm flux
recipe.method: Scale an optically thin modified black body to S_1.3mm and integrate 8-1000 um for L_IR; M_dust = D_L S / (kappa B_nu(T_dust))
key_parameters: T_dust = 40 K; beta = 1.4; kappa_0 = 40 cm2/g at 100 um
assumptions: Optically thin emission because E(B-V) <= 0.1; no CMB correction applied

recipe.goal: measure rest-UV/optical sizes from near-IR imaging
recipe.method: Single 2D Gaussian fit with GALFIT convolved with a PSF measured from bright field stars, on 10''x10'' background-subtracted cutouts; an extra component for J0146-0220 and J0006+2452

recipe.goal: derive SFRs, depletion times, gas fractions and star-formation efficiency and compare with literature relations
recipe.method: SFR_IR = L_IR/1e10 (Kennicutt98, Chabrier IMF); SFR_UV+IR = SFR_UV+SFR_IR; t_depl = M_molgas/SFR_UV+IR; f_molgas = M_molgas/(M_molgas+M_stars); eps_SF = M_stars(young)/(M_molgas+M_stars(young))
assumptions: M_stars from SFR_UV x 10 Myr (dust-corrected with beta_UV), Chabrier IMF, kappa_UV from BPASS binaries at 0.5 Zsun

evidence.quote: The high dust masses $M_{\rm dust} = (2.3-11.1)\times 10^7~M_{\odot}$ of our galaxies
are spread out between $\log (\delta_{\rm DGR}) < -2.9$ and $-2.1$ for $\alpha_{\rm CO}^{\rm SB}$
They reach $\rm SFR_{IR} = 59~M_{\odot}~\rm yr^{-1}$ to $283~M_{\odot}~\rm yr^{-1}$
ranging between $\lesssim 14$% and 42%
considerably above (a factor of $\sim 30$) the main sequence of star-forming galaxies

evidence.loc: Molecular gas mass content and depletion timescale
evidence.quote: range between $M_{\rm molgas} <0.63\times 10^{10}~M_{\odot}$ and $3.67\times 10^{10}~M_{\odot}$

evidence.loc: Molecular gas mass content and depletion timescale
evidence.quote: with a mean of $\rm 49~Myr \pm 12~Myr$ for $\alpha_{\rm CO}^{\rm SB}$
amazingly short $t_{\rm depl}$ between 36 Myr and 71 Myr

evidence.loc: Molecular gas mass content and depletion timescale
evidence.quote: is depleted in $<13$ Myr!

evidence.loc: Molecular gas mass content and depletion timescale
evidence.quote: have very high $f_{\rm molgas}$ with a mean of $82\%\pm 10\%$ for $\alpha_{\rm CO}^{\rm SB}$

evidence.loc: Molecular gas mass content and depletion timescale
evidence.quote: mean molecular gas mass to stellar mass ratio ($\mu_{\rm molgas} = M_{\rm molgas}/M_{\rm stars}$) of $6\pm 3$
with a mean of $18\% \pm 9\%$ for $\alpha_{\rm CO}^{\rm SB}$
We find $\epsilon_{\rm SF}$ ranging from 8% to 37%

evidence.loc: FIR dust continuum and rest-frame UV/optical sizes
evidence.quote: They range between $R_{\rm eff,FIR} = 1.7$ kpc and 5.0 kpc

answer_key.quantity: Mean ratio of rest-UV/optical to FIR effective radius

evidence.loc: FIR dust continuum and rest-frame UV/optical sizes
evidence.quote: the mean $R_{\rm eff,UV/opt}/R_{\rm eff,FIR} =0.43\pm 0.17$ ratio of our galaxies

score_reason: Programme IDs, targets, imaging weighting/pixel size and the derived-quantity recipe (MBB, alpha_CO, r_J1, SFR) are given and numeric results are tabulated, but aperture choices, CASA/pipeline versions, calibrators, masks and companion-paper inputs are missing.
rediscovery_reason: Cycle 6 and Cycle 8 PI data of known project codes are likely public by now (the paper does not state it); the recipe for fluxes, L'_CO, M_molgas, L_IR, M_dust is explicit and results are numeric, though aperture choices would shift values within errors.
